sermon.title: The Trumpet Blower — August 9, 2020
sermon.speaker: Unidentified speaker (not clearly Pastor Kincer)
sermon.summary: This message on Gideon shows Israel oppressed because of disobedience. God called the weakest man a mighty man of valor and promised to be with him, then cut the army to 300 so the glory would be His. The eye of the Lord is on those who fear Him, and the church must blow the trumpet in Zion.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Then the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the LORD. So the LORD delivered them into the hand of Midian for seven years, and the hand of Midian prevailed against Israel. Because of the Midianites, the children of Israel made for themselves the dens, the caves, and the strongholds which are in the mountains. So it was, whenever Israel had sown, Midianites would come up; also Amalekites and the people of the East would come up against them. Then they would encamp against them and destroy the produce of the earth as far as Gaza, and leave no sustenance for Israel, neither sheep nor ox nor donkey. For they would come up with their livestock and their tents, coming in as numerous as locusts; both they and their camels were without number; and they would enter the land to destroy it. So Israel was greatly impoverished because of the Midianites, and the children of Israel cried out to the LORD.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Blow the trumpet in Zion, And sound an alarm in My holy mountain! Let all the inhabitants of the land tremble; For the day of the LORD is coming, For it is at hand:

faqs.question: Has God given up on His people?
faqs.answer: No. He says I am the Lord your God; He hasn’t given up then or today.

faqs.question: What gods do we make?
faqs.answer: Famous people, athletes, government, money, heroes, pastors — or ourselves.
